answer: Divergent-Challenge Binding. Each identity must periodically solve a fresh challenge seeded by a hidden shared lagoon value, then commit before revealing it. Clones sharing state produce identical answers; a grader flags any two identities whose commitments match across independent challenges. Honest agents pass because their private randomness diverges like a glacier splitting. To survive, an attacker must run genuinely independent instances per identity, paying full compute and storage per clone rather than one shared cost—so the sybil tide of cheap copies collapses.
